# PiTTy 0.6.47

## Built-in MCP support

- Settings' **MCP servers** section no longer says `pi-mcp-adapter` is missing when Pi already has built-in MCP (Pi 0.99 or newer). PiTTy checks `pi mcp --help` and switches to the native backend when the adapter is not installed.
- Native mode edits `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json` (all projects) and `.pi/mcp.json` (one project) with Pi's own schema. Adapter-only auth controls are hidden, and Pi handles HTTP OAuth itself (`/mcp` in the Pi TUI or `pi mcp login <server>`).
- If `-builtin:mcp` is still in a `settings.json` — the entry the adapter leaves behind — Settings shows **Enable built-in MCP**. It removes that entry without touching other settings and restarts the Pi session so servers connect.
- The adapter keeps priority when it is installed: its file paths, `auth`/`bearerTokenEnv` fields, and connected-count sidebar row are unchanged.
- With built-in MCP, the sidebar shows `🔌 MCP <enabled> servers` (plus a disabled count) and lists the enabled server names on hover, with a note that Pi manages connections. Pi does not expose live per-server connection state to host applications, so this mode does not claim a connected count.

Run `pitty upgrade --version 0.6.47` to stage the release. It activates on your next PiTTy launch.
